output.title: When search is a workflow decision
output.body:
If you are rethinking search behaviour in a small business, start with one question: are people repeatedly looking through your own business material, or the open web? That difference matters. Repeated searching in customer emails, past invoices, product specs, or help-desk notes is a workflow problem. Random web research usually is not.

For an owner-operator, the useful test is simple: does that repeated internal searching take a noticeable slice of the week and affect response time, errors, or back-and-forth? If yes, treat it as a bounded workflow decision, not a broad AI strategy.

The control is document readiness. A knowledge assistant fits only when the material already exists in machine-readable form, such as MD, PDF, or structured data. Bareni has a self-built demo that retrieves from approved company documents rather than the open web. It runs end to end locally on synthetic data; OCR, scan ingestion, billing, and rate limiting are not working in that demo.

Keep human approval in place when search output affects customer communication or a business decision. The system proposes; you decide. That is Bareni’s policy for high-risk decisions, not an absolute warranty.

One practical next step: map one recurring search task on paper, then check whether the source material is ready and whether you still want final review before anything goes out. If that question comes back as yes, you have a real workflow to discuss.
